html:
SMTO-FIL-0039 — This copy looks like a repeat of one already started

GUID: ec9af8b3-ffa9-4679-b486-0fba777c89d2
Slug: file-transfer-id-reused
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • The Gateway already has a record of a copy with the same internal number, so it refused to start it again. Starting it twice could copy the file twice or mix up the two copies.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO in the conversation to show the size and last-modified time of the file at the destination and of the original file, and compare them. If the destination file is already there and matches, the copy doesn't need to be repeated.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, expand the source and destination Gateways, and compare their addresses and Node names; they should be different computers. If both entries lead to the same Gateway, the receiving half of the copy collides with the sending half.
  3. To copy a file within one computer, ask SMTO to copy it on that single Gateway instead. A copy between Gateways is only meant for two separate computers.
  4. Only if the file is missing, ask SMTO to start a new copy. A new request gets a fresh number, so it won't collide with the old record.

What success looks like

  • The destination file is there and matches the original, or a new copy finishes and is verified.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateways. Don't keep repeating the same request until they've confirmed what happened to the first copy.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway refused source_open, destination_begin or adopt_source because the run/transfer key already exists in its live sessions, recently finished receipts or the node's transfer journal.

What this means

  • The run/transfer identity already exists in active sessions, finished receipts or the durable journal. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The run/transfer identity already exists in active sessions, finished receipts or the durable journal.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original transfer receipt and destination before selecting any new identity.

How to fix it

  • Look up the existing transfer_id with destination_status on the Gateway and settle it (abort, or reconcile any committing/unknown record) before new work, and verify that the source and destination Gateway records do not point at the same Gateway process, which shares one session table. New copies get a fresh random transfer identity; never reuse an old identity to force a replay.
  • Reconcile the existing transfer first; use a fresh identity only for separately intended new work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The original transfer is settled before distinct new work gets a fresh identity.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
